name: Architectural Promenade as Temporally Composed Multi-Modal Prediction Error Trajectory
panel_source: SPATIAL-I (Sprint 13.17) — upgrades SC-I structural YAML (Doc 38) and SC-II partial calibration (Doc 62); SC3 was 'uncalibrated' at SC-I, 'partial' at SC-II, now 'calibrated' with THEORETICAL_DEFAULT flags on key parameters

t1_5_parent_theories.name: Prospect-Refuge (Appleton, 1975)
t1_5_parent_theories.reduction_pathway: The compression phase of compression-release is a refuge extreme; the release phase transitions to a prospect extreme. The emotional power of the sequence derives from the oscillation between these poles — the body's relief at gaining prospect after compression is the affective core of the promenade threshold event.

t1_5_parent_theories.name: ART (Kaplan, 1995)
t1_5_parent_theories.reduction_pathway: The promenade produces fascination (involuntary attention to spatially novel sequences), extent (the building's spatial narrative suggests a whole world beyond the current view), compatibility (the path is traversable, confirming agency), and complexity (varied spatial types maintain engagement). SC3 operationalizes ART's four components in the temporal dimension.

mechanism_chain.description: The architectural promenade is a designed sequence of spatial zones, each with a distinct multi-modal character (spatial volume, luminance, material texture, acoustic absorption, thermal condition). The architect composes the sequence by determining the ORDER, CONTRAST, and TIMING of transitions between zones.

data.finding: Architectural promenade is a designed sequence of spatial zones with distinct modal characters

justification.backing: Step 1 is definitional — the promenade as a compositional concept. The PE interpretation adds predictive processing to Le Corbusier's spatial sequence.
justification.qualifier: Definitional step — the concept of spatial sequence is universally accepted in architectural theory.

mechanism_chain.description: COMPRESSION PHASE: In the compressed zone (low ceiling, narrow width, dim light, absorptive materials, cool temperature), the brain builds strong predictions of CONSTRICTION. Each modality confirms a model of spatial limitation: spatial PE is low (predictions confirmed), but the model being confirmed is one of restriction and limitation. The body registers this through interoceptive monitoring — posture adapts, proprioception detects spatial proximity of surfaces, breathing may shorten.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Somatosensory cortex and posterior insula for body schema in space; entorhinal cortex maintaining spatial model under constrained conditions; orbitofrontal cortex registering low-reward state of confirmed constriction

data.finding: Compression phase: low ceiling, narrow width, dim light → strong predictions of constriction confirmed → low PE but aversive model
data.effect: Body schema adapts to constriction; interoceptive load increases

justification.backing: Ellard defended the Weber-Fechner logarithmic form as grounded in perceptual neuroscience (the form IS what the perceptual system does with proportional change). The coefficient 0.30 ± 0.15 reflects wide CI from small samples. The functional form has confidence 0.70 (MECHANISM); the coefficient has confidence 0.50 (THEORETICAL_DEFAULT with empirical anchoring).
justification.qualifier: Ellard explicitly qualified: "The coefficient 0.30 should be treated as a central estimate with a wide confidence interval (±0.15). The multi-channel bonus values are more speculative — linear interpolations from a single data point."
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) perceptual Weber-Fechner psychophysics does not apply to complex multi-modal architectural transitions because the stimuli are not unidimensional; (b) the GSR response measures general arousal rather than specifically spatial PE — the coefficient captures arousal generically, not the spatial prediction mechanism specifically.

mechanism_chain.description: THRESHOLD EVENT: At the spatial transition (doorway, arch, threshold), MULTIPLE MODALITIES change simultaneously. The compressed spatial prediction is violated across all channels simultaneously. The prediction-error signal is NOT just one channel's mismatch but the CONVERGENT mismatch across spatial, luminance, material, acoustic, and possibly thermal channels — all at once. The convergent multi-channel mismatch drives a large, rapid arousal response (GSR peak, pupil dilation, orienting reflex, brief attentional capture).
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Superior colliculus orienting reflex; locus coeruleus noradrenergic burst (novelty signal); superior temporal sulcus (STS) multi-sensory convergence; amygdala rapid appraisal of whether the sudden environmental change signals threat or positive novelty; dopamine release (VTA-NAcc) if the threshold event confirms a positive prediction (arriving at a desired destination)

data.finding: Multi-modal threshold events produce convergent PE across multiple channels simultaneously
Multi-channel bonus values: spatial+light=0.25, +material=0.40, +acoustic=0.55, all five=0.70 μS

justification.backing: Bermudez EAE data confirm that AX3 (awe) threshold requires spatial + at minimum one additional channel: "Single-channel spatial transitions, however dramatic, do not produce peak architectural experiences." The multi-channel convergence is not optional — it is the GATING condition for peak response (Bermudez, 78% of EAEs involve spatial transition, 65% involve simultaneous light change).
justification.qualifier: Multi-channel bonus confidence 0.40-0.45 (THEORETICAL_DEFAULT). "The actual function could be non-additive" (Ellard). The linear interpolation from Kuliga's single data point is the weakest calibration in SC3. Bermudez provides qualitative confirmation but not parametric validation.
justification.rebuttal: Holl challenged the entire framing: "The buildings that produce the greatest experiences cannot be described by a threshold density number and a compression ratio. What they share is INTENTIONALITY." The claim would fail if: (a) multi-channel convergence is multiplicative rather than additive, producing much larger or smaller effects than linear interpolation predicts; (b) the emotional impact depends on compositional intentionality (Holl) rather than on the number of simultaneously changing channels.

competing_accounts.claim: The emotional power of architectural thresholds depends on compositional placement and narrative arc, not on counting how many sensory channels change simultaneously
competing_accounts.implication_for_template: If intentionality dominates, the multi-channel bonus is a necessary but insufficient condition. The Holl temporal shape becomes the primary predictor, with channel count as a secondary enabler. SC3 was revised to make Holl temporal shape a REQUIRED MODIFIER.

mechanism_chain.description: RELEASE PHASE: In the released zone (high ceiling, broad width, bright daylight, reverberant materials), all channels confirm the new model of spatial generosity. The contrast between the BUILT expectation (from compression) and the REVEALED reality (the release) drives the emotional response. The stronger the compression, the more complete the expected constriction model, and therefore the greater the violation at release. This is why long, extreme compression sequences produce stronger release responses: they build a more precise and confident constriction model.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Orbitofrontal cortex positive value signal; hippocampal place cell ensemble update to new spatial context; beta-endorphin and oxytocin release consistent with relief from sustained constraint (speculative — no direct architectural measurement); PPA scene update to high-valued scene type

data.finding: Orbitofrontal cortex positive value signal at contrast resolution; hippocampal place cell update to new spatial context
data.source: Theoretical integration from predictive coding + reward neuroscience
data.effect: Relief from sustained constraint → positive affect

data.finding: Longer compression sequences produce stronger release responses
data.source: Ellard ambulatory observations; Bermudez EAE data
data.effect: Compression duration correlates with release magnitude

justification.backing: The release phase generates positive affect through: (a) contrast between built expectation (constriction model) and revealed reality (spatial generosity) — the bigger the mismatch, the bigger the response; (b) relief from interoceptive constriction load (IC2 pathway). "The stronger the compression, the more complete the expected constriction model, and therefore the greater the violation at release."
justification.qualifier: Confidence at this step is moderate. The mechanism is well-articulated but the specific neural pathway (OFC value signal + hippocampal context update) is theoretical — no study has measured OFC and hippocampal activity during an architectural compression-release sequence.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) the release response is primarily relief (return to baseline) rather than genuine positive affect — the distinction matters for whether buildings should design for compression-release or simply for consistently generous spaces; (b) any compressed space in sequence works, or only compositionally intentional ones (Holl critique).

mechanism_chain.description: TEMPORAL COMPOSITION: The emotional trajectory of the promenade depends on both the MAGNITUDE of PE at each threshold and the TEMPORAL DENSITY of thresholds. The Goldilocks zone (20–45 seconds between significant thresholds at typical walking pace) maintains GSR responsivity without habituation or fatigue. Holl's compositional temporal shape specifies position-weighted density: approach (low density, anticipation building) → development (moderate, rhythmic engagement) → climax (high density + maximum contrast) → denouement (very low, resolution).
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Anterior temporal cortex narrative construction (the brain constructs a NARRATIVE of the spatial sequence, with the same temporal prediction mechanisms used for story comprehension — Hasson et al., 2008); hippocampal theta rhythm entrainment to walking rhythm organizes episodic chunking at threshold events; DMN deactivation during active exploration with periodic reactivation during pause-for-integration moments

data.finding: Threshold density Goldilocks zone: 20-45 seconds between significant events at walking pace
data.source: Ellard ambulatory data; Holl compositional theory
data.effect: Peak engagement at 20-45s interval; habituation >60s; fatigue <15s

data.finding: Holl temporal shape: approach (0.5), development (0.8), climax (1.5), denouement (0.4) position weights

justification.backing: Ellard and Holl reached consensus: "the GSR function gives the MAGNITUDE response; the Holl temporal shape gives the WEIGHTING by position in the compositional arc." The combined model: effective_response = GSR_peak(isovist_ratio, multi-channel_bonus) × position_weight(phase). Holl accepted position weights as "reasonable first approximations" with ±0.3 precision.
justification.qualifier: Threshold density confidence 0.45 (THEORETICAL_DEFAULT). Position weights (±0.30) are compositional estimates, not measured. "I would not claim precision beyond ±0.3 for any of them" (Holl). The direction is confirmed: climax position amplifies; approach position dampens.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) temporal composition is too variable across building types and occupant populations to parameterize — different cultures may have different temporal rhythm preferences; (b) the Goldilocks zone (20-45s) is an artifact of Ellard's stimulus set and does not generalize to other building types.

mechanism_chain.description: PARTIAL REVELATION: The architectural device of revealing the next space THROUGH a narrow opening before the threshold is crossed creates anticipatory prediction error — the brain begins generating predictions about the release space before arriving, extending the emotional ramp. This accounts for 32% of EAE reports (Bermudez, 2009) and adds approximately 0.15–0.25 μS to the effective GSR area under the response curve by extending the duration of elevated arousal.
mechanism_chain.neural_substrate: Spatial working memory maintaining the partial scene model; anticipatory dopaminergic signaling when a rewarding space is predicted but not yet reached (Schultz, 1997); visual cortex predictive completion of the partially-revealed space

data.finding: 32% of EAE reports describe partial revelation — seeing the destination through a narrow opening before entering
Anticipatory dopaminergic signaling when rewarding space is predicted but not yet reached
data.effect: DA neurons fire at reward prediction, not just reward delivery

justification.backing: The partial revelation device extends the threshold event over time. Bermudez: "the GSR response begins at the point of first visibility, not at the physical crossing." Ellard confirmed: "Duration of elevated GSR is greater, even if peak magnitude is similar. The bonus reflects increased AREA under the GSR curve." The Schultz DA mechanism provides the neural grounding: reward anticipation.
justification.qualifier: Confidence 0.40 (THEORETICAL_DEFAULT). The partial revelation bonus (+0.15-0.25 μS area under curve) is estimated from EAE prevalence + physiological inference, not directly measured.
justification.rebuttal: The claim would fail if: (a) partial revelation reduces rather than amplifies the threshold response by dissipating surprise — seeing the space ahead means the full reveal is less surprising; (b) the 32% EAE prevalence of partial revelation is correlation, not causation — the buildings that use partial revelation are also the ones with the most compositional care overall.

spatial_configuration.construct: Peak GSR response at spatial threshold as a function of isovist area ratio (release / compression)

coefficient.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — empirically anchored but scaling coefficient has wide CI (±0.15). Weber-Fechner extrapolation from VR (N=48, Kuliga) + ambulatory data (Ellard, N=40 buildings). Needs larger N and cross-cultural replication.

first_visit.modifier: +0.05 to +0.10 μS — predictions are less established; violations more surprising

familiar_building.modifier: -0.10 to -0.15 μS — promenade PE reduced with familiarity; the sequence becomes an ANTICIPATED pleasure rather than a genuine surprise

visual_complexity.construct: Additive effect of partial-revelation device (viewing next space through narrow opening before threshold crossing) on emotional response area under curve
visual_complexity.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — 32% EAE prevalence (Bermudez) + Ellard mechanism inference; no direct measurement of the anticipatory extension
visual_complexity.bridge_warrant: MECHANISM — anticipatory dopaminergic signaling to predicted reward (Schultz, 1997) provides neural basis; the architectural device is a direct instantiation of the predictive-reward mechanism

architectural_threshold.construct: Interval between significant threshold events (seconds at typical walking pace 1.2 m/s) for optimal sustained engagement

too_sparse.effect: Habituation — GSR baseline drifts down; self-report shifts to 'monotonous'

optimal.effect: Maintained GSR responsivity; peak self-reported engagement
optimal.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — Ellard ambulatory data; needs controlled study (Prediction 1 from SC-II)

architectural_threshold.architectural_distance_at_1.2ms: Optimal spacing: 24–54 meters between significant thresholds

temporal_rhythm.construct: Position-weight modulating the emotional magnitude of a threshold based on its location in the promenade arc
temporal_rhythm.flag: THEORETICAL_DEFAULT — Holl compositional principles + Bermudez EAE data; position weight values are first approximations (±0.30); controlled VR study needed (Prediction 4 from SC-II)
temporal_rhythm.bridge_warrant: FUNCTIONAL — same temporal optimization principles as musical composition (expectancy-tension-resolution); direct mapping to PP framework is theoretically strong but specific position weights are extrapolated

ie_dpt_interaction.implicit: T_IE_005 (Aesthetic Affect) — the implicit channel generates an immediate affective response at each threshold before explicit evaluation; the GSR spike is partly this implicit aesthetic-surprise response
ie_dpt_interaction.explicit: T_IE_009 (Narrative Construction) — the explicit channel constructs a narrative of the spatial sequence; visitors who explicitly attend to the compositional arc report higher appreciation of the promenade as a whole; Kirsh's sense of 'explicit' as available to deliberate manipulation applies — the visitor can choose to attend to the sequence as composition

primary: Museums and galleries (promenade IS the curatorial medium)
secondary: Luxury hospitality (hotel arrival sequence, spa approach)
High-quality workplace headquarters (arrival and atrium sequences)
low_applicability: Utilitarian buildings where occupants random-access rather than promenade (most offices, standard healthcare)
Retail environments (movement optimization, not emotional composition — though some luxury retail uses promenade logic)

interaction_with_LUM_CONTRAST_PE_001.note: SC3 depends on L1 (LUM_CONTRAST_PE_001) for luminance PE at thresholds. The multi-channel convergence bonus assumes L1 parameters are independently computed and then combined additively. LUM_CONTRAST_PE_001 is currently assigned to VISUAL-I per §7 of the transfer document (Finding 1, Session 7). SC3's calibration is complete PENDING L1 calibration from VISUAL-I. Until LUM_CONTRAST_PE_001 is calibrated, Article Eater should use SC-II's luminance bonus values (+0.25 for spatial+light channel) as the temporary L1 proxy in SC3.

panel_reasoning_excerpt:
### Template SC2: Isovist Dynamics and Visual Prediction Horizon

```yaml
template_id: "ISOVIST_VISUAL_PREDICTION_001"
display_id: "SC2"
name: "Isovist Properties as Visual Prediction Range and Spatial Monitoring Capacity"

structural_pattern: >
  The isovist at any point in a building — the total volume of space
  visible from that point — defines the visual prediction range: the
  region within which the brain can base spatial predictions on direct
  sensory evidence rather than inference. Isovist properties determine
  the quality of environmental monitoring. Large isovist area → wide
  prediction range → confident spatial model, effective threat
  assessment (T5), low spatial uncertainty. Small isovist area →
  narrow prediction range → uncertain spatial model, limited threat
  assessment, high spatial uncertainty. Occluding edges at the isovist
  boundary define the limits of perception and the onset of prediction:
  beyond each occluding edge, the brain must infer what lies hidden,
  generating spatial expectations that may be confirmed or violated
  upon movement.
  
  As the occupant moves through the building, the isovist changes
  continuously (isovist drift). Smooth drift (gentle curves, gradual
  reveals) produces continuous, moderate spatial PE — the prediction
  horizon shifts incrementally and the brain updates smoothly. Sharp
  drift (turning a corner, passing through a doorway) produces
  discontinuous PE — the prediction horizon snaps to a new
  configuration and the brain must rapidly construct a new spatial
  model. The RATE of isovist change along a movement path determines
  the temporal density of spatial PE events.
  
  Prospect-refuge theory (Appleton, 1975) maps directly onto isovist
  properties: prospect = large isovist area in the forward direction;
  refuge = small isovist area at the back and overhead (the body is
  partially concealed). The evolved preference for prospect-refuge
  balance IS a preference for a specific isovist configuration — one
  that maximizes visual prediction range in the direction of potential
  threat (forward) while minimizing the visual access of potential
  threats to the self (behind, above).

higher_order_principle: >
  The visual instantiation of spatial prediction. As SC1 describes
  the navigational prediction structure of the spatial network
  (topological), SC2 describes the perceptual prediction structure
  at each point (geometric). SC1 operates on the cognitive map; SC2
  operates on the visual field. They are complementary: a navigator
  uses both the local isovist (what can I see right now?) and the
  cognitive map (what lies beyond what I can see?) to form spatial
  predictions. SC2 also connects directly to T5 (threat/safety):
  the isovist determines what the visual system can monitor for
  threats, and the prospect-refuge preference is an evolved
  optimization of the isovist for survival.

framework_ids:
  - "space_syntax"
  - "visual_graph_analysis"
  - "prospect_refuge_theory"
  - "predictive_processing"
  - "threat_monitoring"

IC2_body_budget.interaction: The compression phase creates an interoceptive load — spatial constriction is registered through the body (posture, proprioception, reduced breathing volume). This is IC2 being PRIMED: the body budget anticipates a demand that the release then lifts. The emotional relief at the release is partly an interoceptive signal — the body's prediction of ongoing constriction is violated, and the body updates to a lower-demand state. SC3 is one of the few templates where IC2 is explicitly involved in the MECHANISM of the emotional response, not merely downstream.
IC2_body_budget.direction: SC3 and IC2 co-participate at threshold events; compression primes IC2 allostatic demand which release resolves

AX4_perceived_control.interaction: The promenade is AX4-positive when the threshold sequence is DESIGNED — when the visitor experiences spatial transitions as composed revelations rather than spatial confusion. The sense that the architect intended these transitions, and that the visitor is reading the spatial narrative, is a form of perceived control (interpretive agency). Buildings where the promenade sequence is opaque (no legible compositional logic) convert the same PE events from positive AX4 (discovery) to negative AX4 (disorientation). Intent-legibility of the spatial composition is the AX4 lever in SC3.
AX4_perceived_control.direction: SC3 outcome (positive vs. negative) is AX4-modulated by visitor's ability to perceive compositional intentionality
